intro: Learn vocabulary for the extended family and marital status with estar: casado, soltero, abuelos, tíos, primos, and nietos.
b1.titulo: The wider family and marital status
b1.texto:
The masculine plural covers both genders: **los abuelos** are grandfather and grandmother, **los tíos** uncle and aunt, and **los hijos** sons and daughters.

In Spanish we use **de** to indicate family relationships: *el padre de mi madre es mi abuelo*.

To talk about marital status we usually use the verb **estar** with adjectives agreeing in gender: **estoy casado / casada**, **está soltero / soltera**.

To ask questions we say: *¿Estás casado?*, *¿Tienes hijos?*. And reply: *Tengo dos hijos: un hijo y una hija*.

For relative age we use **mayor** (older) and **menor** (younger): *mi hermano mayor*.
b4.texto:
The marital status adjective agrees with the person we are speaking about:

- **Masculine**: Pablo está casado.
- **Feminine**: Lucía está casada.

Use *soltero / soltera* for people who are not married.
b5.f0.texto: Pablo's lovely grandparents live in a truly picturesque and pleasant village.
b5.f1.texto: They own a very large stone house surrounded by tall green leafy trees.
b5.f2.texto: The entire family gathers together every summer with immense heartfelt joy.
b5.f3.texto: My uncles are extraordinarily friendly and have two cheerful, playful children.
b5.f4.texto: My cousins always play happily together across the spacious green garden lawn.
b5.f5.texto: All of us gladly share the hearty homemade meal around the long table.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: your mother's or father's brother is your uncle (tío).
b6.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: your uncle's son is your cousin (primo).
b6.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: your parents' father is your grandfather (abuelo).
b7.pregunta: Complete the sentence with the correct word.
b7.frase: Los padres de mi padre son mis ___.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: your father's parents are your grandparents (abuelos).
b7.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: tíos are uncles and aunts.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I have two children».
p.los abuelos.consejo: Masculine plural including grandfather and grandmother.
p.el tío.consejo: Your parent's brother. Has an accent on the i.
p.la tía.consejo: Your parent's sister. Has an accent on the i.
p.los tíos.consejo: Plural referring to uncles and aunts together.
p.el primo.consejo: Son of your uncle or aunt.
p.la prima.consejo: Daughter of your uncle or aunt.
p.el nieto.consejo: Son of your son or daughter.
p.el sobrino.consejo: Son of your brother or sister.
p.la sobrina.consejo: Daughter of your brother or sister.
p.el marido.consejo: Married man in relation to his spouse.
p.la mujer.consejo: Married woman (wife) or woman in general.
p.casado.consejo: Marital status adjective used with estar.
p.casada.consejo: Feminine marital status adjective with estar.
p.marido.consejo: Its partner word for a wife is «esposa». The r between vowels is a quick tap: ma-RI-do.
p.hijos.consejo: The h is silent and the j sounds like «h»: I-hos. The singular is «hijo».
p.abuelos.consejo: The ue is one stressed syllable: a-BWE-los. The singular is «abuelo».
p.nietos.consejo: The singular is «nieto», stressed on the first syllable. The ie sounds like «ye»: NYE-tos.
p.muchos.consejo: Its feminine form is «muchas», used before feminine nouns like «casas». The ch sounds as in «chocolate».
p.primos.consejo: «primos» is the plural of «primo»; the final -s means there are several of them.
p.árboles.consejo: «árboles» is the plural of «árbol». The accent on «ár» shows the stress is on the first syllable.
p.altos.consejo: «alto» means tall; «altos» ends in -os because it agrees with the plural «árboles».
p.reúne.consejo: The tilde on «ú» splits the vowels: «re-ú-ne» has three syllables, not two.
p.verano.consejo: One soft r between vowels: a quick tap, not the rolled «rr» of «perro».
p.tíos.consejo: The tilde on «í» splits «tí-os» into two syllables; «tía» means aunt.
p.alegres.consejo: «alegre» is the singular; «alegres» is the plural, matching the children, «hijos».
p.juegan.consejo: «juego», a game, shares the same root. The «j» sounds like a soft English «h».
p.compartimos.consejo: The «c» before «o» sounds like «k», and the stress falls on «ti» in «com-par-TI-mos».
p.larga.consejo: «larga» agrees with «mesa», which is feminine, so the ending changes from -o to -a.
p.tío.consejo: Its feminine is «tía», and the plural «tíos» can mean uncles and aunts together.
